tables.name: adult_auricle_length_width
tables.units: mm (cm values converted x10); width_over_length dimensionless
tables.population: Adults; North Indian, Sundanese (Indonesia), and a mixed n=200 sample; sample sizes for North Indian and Sundanese not stated in harvested results
tables.notes: Each row is single-source from harvester search summaries; not yet independently verified. width_over_length is a ratio of means computed by this note, not reported by the sources. Rows differ by population and by measurement definition. Sundanese women's concha width (0.42 cm) omitted as a suspected typo. Lower Sundanese ratio may partly reflect profile foreshortening of width in photogrammetry (hypothesis).

tables.name: male_auricle_height_range_review
tables.population: Young adult males across several published studies
tables.notes: Aggregator topic page; length measured from most superior to most inferior projection. Absolute widths not given, only an approximately 12 mm spread between studies.

tables.name: ear_length_age_change_adult
rows: length increase per year after maturity (mm/yr)
tables.notes: Verified 2026-11-20: Heathcote, BMJ 1995, 'Why do old men have big ears?', cross-sectional 0.22 mm/yr (one source). Conflicts with the 'size and shape steady until ~70' claim relayed by arXiv 2101.10540. Length matures by ~14 (PubMed 29169692, Chinese sample).

tables.name: prominent_ear_thresholds
tables.notes: Exact upper/lower measurement points not given in harvested summary. The same study suggests the otoplasty success criterion of <3 mm asymmetry may be too strict.

tables.name: auriculocephalic_angle_norms
tables.notes: Two norms differ; harvester could not confirm that the 20-30 degree figure maps to this exact page. Measurement methods differ between studies (ruler, photo, 3D plane-normal).

tables.name: otoplasty_aesthetic_goals_and_fold_angles
rows: surgical target (called too strict by PubMed 22067874)
tables.notes: Expert knowledge: McDowell, 'Goals in otoplasty for protruding ears', Plast Reconstr Surg 1968, and standard otoplasty teaching. Angles given as approximate ranges around the usually quoted ~90 degrees. Not yet verified.

tables.name: ear_position_orientation_FH_frame
tables.units: mm unless stated; head in Frankfort horizontal
rows: tragion height minus soft-tissue orbitale height
tragion position along ear height, fraction from superaurale
superaurale height minus brow lower edge (mid-pupil)
subaurale height minus subnasale height (negative = below)
long-axis tilt back from FH vertical
ear length minus nose height n-sn
tables.population: Adults; mostly European-descent conventions and anthropometric teaching
tables.notes: Expert knowledge, not yet verified; 'spread' is a suggested 1-sigma, not a measured SD. Brow and subnasale alignments and nasal-dorsum parallelism are canons that Farkas (1985 canon revision; Anthropometry of the Head and Face, 1994) found only approximately or rarely true; use as UI warnings, not energy terms. Subaurale sits lower with age.

tables.name: subfeature_planning_ranges
rows: total ear thickness at helix rim
tables.notes: Rough sculpting ranges from expert knowledge, not anthropometric norms. Verify against Farkas (1994) or a 3D ear dataset before use as priors.

tables.name: photo_geometry_ear_scale_factors
rows: frontal: ear scale relative to nose-tip scale
profile: near-ear scale relative to midsagittal profile
tables.population: Pinhole-camera geometry with typical adult offsets
tables.notes: Computed: frontal = D/(D+110 mm); profile = D/(D-80 mm). Offsets are approximate (nose tip to ear-plane depth ~100-130 mm; ear ~70-90 mm lateral of midline). Pitch effect: ear-vs-brow vertical shift ~100 mm x sin(pitch) (~9 mm at 5 deg, ~17 mm at 10 deg; chin-down makes ears look higher). True-profile width foreshortening ~cos(flare) = 0.82-0.94.

tables.name: suggested_fitting_priors
rows: ratio of means 0.47-0.54 in sourced rows
soft symmetry; McDowell 3 mm goal, called too strict
tables.notes: Length and width priors derive from sourced means; tilt, tragion, age slope and symmetry sigmas are expert knowledge. Replace with verified population tables when available; keep population tag.
